newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Steel&Tube to shed jobs at subsidiary-paper.
newsitem.headline: Steel&Tube to shed jobs at subsidiary-paper.

text.p: Steel and Tube Holdings plans to cut jobs at subsidiary Southern Cross Engineering in the wake of a weaker group profit for the year ending May 1997, Wellington's Evening Post newspaper reported on Wednesday.
Steel and Tube's tax-paid profit was NZ$19.6 million for the 11 months to May 31, $5.7 million less than the previous 12 months.
Its balance date has been changed to match Australian parent Broken Hill Proprietary.
Southern Cross, which has engineering plants in Hamilton and Christchurch, is a recent acquisition, along with Canadian steel distributor A J Forsyth.
Steel and Tube chief executive Nick Calavrias said Southern Cross needed to become more efficient and some jobs at the Hamilton and Christchurch plants would go in the next year.
The company employed about 100 people. He could not say how many jobs would be lost.
"It's too early to say, but it will be to levels that reflect the work we have on," Calavrias told the paper.
A weaker New Zealand economy had led to lower profits.
But A J Forsyth had increased its profit during the past 11 months despite a flat economy in Canada, he said.
Steel and Tube would concentrate on consolidating its business and was not considering any further acquisitions.
Calavrias said overall he was happy with sales, but profitability levels needed to be improved.
Steel and Tube's directors said trading conditions for the remainder of the calendar year were likely to continue to be weak, although they expected some recovery in the first half of 1998.
Steel and Tube sales for the shortened year to the new balance date of May 31 were up $31.9 million to $387 million, primarily due to inclusion of the acquisitions.
A tax-paid 20 cent a share final dividend has been declared, maintaining the total payout, excluding the bonus issue, at 40c for the year.

The directors have also declared a taxable bonus share for every ordinary share on issue at September 12, 1997. For tax purposes the bonus issue will be treated as a dividend in the hands of shareholders at a gross value of $1 a share, the company said.
The directors said 44 million bonus shares would be allotted on September 19, 1997.
At balance date, total shareholders' funds was up from $121.2 million to $124.2 million.
